newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Beiersdorf restructuring hits profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Beiersdorf restructuring hits profits.

text.p: Beiersdorf AG, the German toiletries and adhesive tape-maker best known for its Nivea skin care range, said on Thursday it expected higher sales this year but restructuring costs would slash earnings.
The company posted sales of 3.24 billion marks for the first six months of the year, up from 3.01 billion marks in the year-ago period.

However its net profit dropped to 85.9 million marks from 140.4 million and the company said restructuring measures at its Tesa adhesive tape division would burden its earnings for the full year by 100 million marks.
Full-year sales would rise by five to seven percent, marking a slight weakening from 1996 when sales rose 8.2 percent to 5.78 billion marks. Net profit in 1996 was 233.8 million marks.
Beiersdorf also said its staff levels had fallen to 18,023 at the end of June from 18,696 at the end of 1996.
Earlier this year, Beiersdorf said it needed to undertake extensive restructuring measures to streamline the group's portfolio and focus its activities on a smaller number of business areas.
Like many German consumer care companies, Beiersdorf has been hurt by the country's sluggish economic development and slowdown in consumer demand.
